stemMd: Why can solid sodium chloride be brittle despite strong attraction between its ions?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The sodium atoms contain no nuclei.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Its ions have no electrical charge in the solid.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The solid consists only of isolated noninteracting molecules.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A displacement can bring like charges next to one another, causing repulsion and fracture.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Every ionic bond turns into a metallic bond when tapped.

explanationMd: Ionic crystals have regular arrangements of alternating charges. Shifting one part of the lattice can align like charges, creating strong repulsion across a plane and causing fracture. Strong bonding therefore does not imply that a material can deform plastically like a metal.

distractorRationale.b: The lattice is held together by charged ions.
distractorRationale.e: Mechanical stress does not normally transform the solid into a metal.
distractorRationale.c: Sodium chloride forms an extended ionic lattice.
